m01.title: Paste the client's message
m01.desc: Fixed rules read the amount and the due date, and fill the form. No AI; nothing is signed or sent.

m02.title: The invoice is a signature
m02.desc: The seller reads the exact values and signs in the wallet: no transaction, no gas.

m03.title: The client pays in MUSD
m03.desc: Four checks, then one signature and one transaction from the client's wallet. The network fee is paid in BTC.

m04.title: A receipt that checks itself
m04.desc: Each time it opens, the receipt verifies the payment on Mezo testnet.

m05.title: Was I really paid?
m05.desc: The real hash of the wave 1 payment, pasted with its payee's wallet: the chain answers, never the message.

m06.title: “I paid you yesterday”
m06.desc: A message the chain cannot check is no proof: ask the client for the hash or the receipt link.

problem.html:
Antananarivo, Madagascar · survey, Oct 28–30, 2026

Getting paid from abroad mostly works.
Trust is what is left.

10Malagasy developers answered, from one Facebook group
9were paid from abroad in the last 12 months
8 of 9say their last payment from abroad went fine

What still hurts: proof that the money really arrived, fake proofs and “I paid” messages,
and a trusted conversion to ariary.

A small, self-selected sample: it does not represent Malagasy freelancers.
